disturbance: A status defined by the authority's own ledger as lasting no more than 45 days has been assigned to the same 61 units continuously since at least January 2022, and only a small fraction of those units show any inspection or repair activity in that time.

hidden_mechanism.claim: A status created to describe a brief administrative pause is, through indefinite renewal and a reporting rule that counts it as occupancy, converted into a permanent removal from the accessible-unit waitlist without that removal ever being recorded as one.
hidden_mechanism.epistemic_status: This is validated EDITORIAL INTERPRETATION, not a quoted source fact. Treat it as the discovery the evidence should be allowed to make intelligible — not a slogan the article must state, open with, close with, or prove like a thesis.

source_anchor: for the duration of a unit inspection or repair, not to exceed 45 days

supporting_evidence.source_excerpt: 61 have carried the internal code "Priority B — Temporary Hold" continuously since at least January 2022
supporting_evidence.editorial_note: the duration the status has actually run, against its own 45-day definition

supporting_evidence.source_excerpt: only 9 of the 61 units under Priority B have had any inspection or repair logged in the past two years
supporting_evidence.editorial_note: shows the status is not tracking what it claims to track

supporting_evidence.source_excerpt: units under administrative hold are counted as occupied for reporting purposes, consistent with standard practice
supporting_evidence.editorial_note: the written rule that does the actual work of hiding the units, and its claim to be standard practice

carrying_material.source_excerpt: told the authority's oversight board in February that he had called about a Priority B unit on Delancey Street four separate times since 2022 and been told each time that the unit was temporarily unavailable, not for the waitlist
carrying_material.editorial_note: a person repeatedly hitting the same status from outside it, over years — treat as one sustained pattern, not a single anecdote

carrying_material.source_excerpt: The board's own annual compliance report, filed with the state in December, lists all 214 units as available accessible inventory without mentioning Priority B at all
carrying_material.editorial_note: the report erases the category entirely, rather than merely mis-defining it

carrying_material.source_excerpt: in a letter dated January 14, why the vacancy rate for accessible units appeared to be zero for three consecutive years despite an average 18-month waitlist, the authority's written response, dated January 29
carrying_material.editorial_note: a two-week question-and-answer sequence is a stronger narrative spine than the raw 61/214 ratio alone -- open on this, not the ratio
no document reviewed says who first proposed counting Priority B units as occupied, or when -- this gap is stronger left open than guessed at

known_gaps: The evidence does not establish who first proposed counting Priority B units as occupied for state reporting, or when that practice began.
The evidence does not establish whether any other housing authority uses a comparable practice.
The evidence does not establish Marcus Oyelaran's current housing status.
The evidence does not establish anyone's knowledge, intent, or state of mind regarding the Priority B practice.
The evidence does not establish any legal conclusion about how long a hold may lawfully last -- only the authority's own policy definition of 45 days.
reader_contract: A report can say zero vacancies for three straight years and be telling the truth about its own paperwork while telling nothing like the truth about the apartments.
form_suggestion: essay -- a document-and-letter sequence carries this more naturally than a portrait or a present-tense field note; Marcus Oyelaran's calls are one strong carrying detail inside the sequence, not a sustained portrait subject
